gaps.sentence: 'Do you know the way?' she asked me. She asked me ___ the way.
gaps.explanation: Do you know → if I knew: no do-support in the reported clause.

gaps.sentence: 'The earth goes round the sun,' the teacher said. The teacher said that the earth ___ round the sun.
gaps.explanation: Timeless general truths may keep the present simple after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll definitely pay you back,' he said. He ___ to pay me back.
gaps.explanation: Promises take promise + to-infinitive: promised to pay me back.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave the building immediately!' the firefighter ordered. The firefighter ordered us ___ the building immediately.
gaps.explanation: Orders are reported with order + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: The colonel ___ his soldiers to advance at dawn.
gaps.explanation: Order + object + to-infinitive reports a command; suggest and hope do not take object + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I moved here two years ago,' he explained. He explained that he had moved there two years ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Ago' becomes 'before' (or 'earlier') in reported speech; here → there as well.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't leave your belongings unattended,' the announcement repeated. The announcement ___ passengers not to leave their belongings unattended.
gaps.hint: warn sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: The warning fits warn + object + not to + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I really must have that report by five,' the editor said. The editor ___ on having the report by five.
gaps.explanation: Insisting on a demand: insist on + -ing (or insist that + clause).
